newsitem.title: CANADA: Sherritt stock falls after debenture issue.
newsitem.headline: Sherritt stock falls after debenture issue.

text.p: Sherritt International Corp shares dropped in heavy trading on Tuesday as investors adjusted their positions after a C$300 million convertible debenture issue, analysts said.
Shares in the nickel company fell 1.15 to 8.25, topping Toronto Stock Exchange actives on almost 3.8 million shares in early trading. Sherritt announced the debenture issue Monday.
"You get a lot of overtrading any time you get a new convertible issue coming in," said mining analyst Manford Mallory with Research Capital Corp.
"If you're already a holder, you may be selling to buy the new issue."
On Monday, Sherritt said it entered an underwriting agreement to issue C$300 million of 6.0 percent, 10-year convertible debentures. The conversion price will be C$9.50.
"A lot of people were taken with the magnitude of the new issue," Mallory said.
Sherritt shares closed at 9.40 in Toronto on Monday, making the premium on the convertible debentures C$0.10.
"Usually there's more of a premium than that," said one mining analyst. "There had to be some adjustment here and the common share is doing the adjusting."
Sherritt said it planned to use proceeds from the offering to expand its projects in Cuba.
Sherritt's main Cuban investment is nickel, but the company said it planned to increase its involvement in the island's sugar, petroleum refining, real estate and communications industries.

Although Sherritt is one of the main targets of the U.S. Helms-Burton law against foreign investment in Cuba, investors were probably not selling their Sherritt stock because of the company's increased exposure on the island, analysts said.
